title: What is a Dual Special Needs plan (D-SNP)?
summary: Introduces Dual Special Needs plans for people with both Medicare and Medicaid: what they are, how they work with Medicaid, care coordination, UnitedHealthcare Dual Complete and the UCard.

assets.alt: Hero image for What is a Dual Special Needs plan

atoms.title: What a Dual Special Needs plan is
atoms.question: What is a Dual Special Needs plan (D-SNP)?
atoms.text: A Dual Special Needs plan, or D-SNP for short, is a type of health insurance plan for people who have both Medicare and Medicaid. If that describes you, you're dual-eligible, which is just another way of saying you can have Medicare and Medicaid at the same time.
questions: Can I have Medicare and Medicaid at the same time?

atoms.title: Who D-SNPs are designed for
atoms.question: Who are Dual Special Needs plans for?
atoms.text: Dual Special Needs plans are for people who could use more help. That may be because of income, disabilities, age and/or health conditions. Dual Special Needs plans are a type of Medicare Advantage plan.
questions: Is a D-SNP a Medicare Advantage plan?
Who should consider a Dual Special Needs plan?

atoms.title: D-SNPs work together with your Medicaid plan
atoms.question: How does dual coverage work with both Medicaid and Medicare?
atoms.text: A Dual Special Needs plan works together with your Medicaid health plan, and you keep all your Medicaid benefits. Most dual health insurance plans also give you more benefits and features than you get with Original Medicare. Dual Special Needs plans have a $0 premium for members with Extra Help (Low Income Subsidy).
questions: Do I keep my Medicaid benefits with a D-SNP?
How much does a D-SNP cost per month?

atoms.title: Personal care coordinator with a D-SNP
atoms.question: What is care coordination in a Dual Special Needs plan?
atoms.text: Care coordination is another important benefit of a Dual Special Needs plan. You'll have a personal care coordinator who may help you understand your Medicare and Medicaid benefits, manage your doctors, specialists and care services, and get the services you need to feel healthier.
questions: Do dual plans include a care coordinator?
Who helps me manage my doctors with Medicare and Medicaid?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare Dual Complete plans
atoms.question: How can I get a Dual Special Needs plan from UnitedHealthcare?
atoms.text: Dual Special Needs plans are offered by private insurance companies, including UnitedHealthcare. UnitedHealthcare calls its dual-eligible health plans UnitedHealthcare Dual Complete. The page states that more people choose UnitedHealthcare for a Dual Special Needs plan than any other company.

atoms.title: UCard for dual plan members
atoms.question: What is the UCard for dual plan members?
atoms.text: UCard is only from UnitedHealthcare. Your UCard is your member ID and more: you can use it to buy healthy food and over-the-counter (OTC) products and to pay utility bills.
questions: What can I buy with the UCard?
Is the UCard my member ID?
